newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget deadline missed, talks set to resume.
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget deadline missed, talks set to resume.

text.p: California lawmakers will resume their fiscal year 1997-1998 budget talks on Monday, stretching deliberations beyond the state's June 15 Constitutional budget deadline.
The legislature's budget conference committee -- made up of three senators and three assembly members -- was scheduled to hold hearings daily until an agreement was reached.

The committee's goal was to meld the budget packages of the state Assembly and Senate into a single spending plan before June 15, the deadline for the state legislature to approve the budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1.
In recent years, however, the June 15 deadline has regularly been missed.
Gov. Pete Wilson and leaders of the state Senate and Assembly, known collectively as the "Big Five," were scheduled to hold their next budget meeting on June 19.

The Big Five lawmakers met for less than an hour last week. Their June 19 talks are expected to center on this year's most hotly disputed legislative issues -- welfare reform, tax cuts and school funding.
